newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Aug 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Aug 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Economic indicators in the first half were positive but do not reflect the right picture of the country's business environment.
- French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux in charge of Casablanca city water and waste treatment is finally operational.
- Morocco's leisure activity reached in value 9.1 billion dirhams ($910 million) or four percent of the country's total consumption.
- French tourism giant Club Mediterrannee to launch an agressive price campaign in Morocco.
- More than a dozen ministers with political affiliation to leave the cabinet of Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and will be replaced soon.
- State-owned Office National de l'Electricite to invest 2.5 billion dirhams on a two-year period to downsize energy costs.
- Foreign investments rose to 6.0 billion dirhams in the first half with a lion-share held by Asian investors, including South Korean conglomerate Daewoo.
- State-owned Regie des Tabacs to invest 70 million dirhams in a tobacco cultivation project in remote northern area of Al-Hoceima.

- Differences over liberalisation of air transportation. The authorities agree on opening the capital of Morocco's airlines Royal Air Maroc to privates but its floation on the bourse remains suspended.
- Giant Office Cherifien des Phosphates exports of phosphates and by-products rose 33.6 percent in the first half of the year.
- Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali to head a third government since February 1995 and conduct election process until the end.
